By leveraging flexible antenna reconfiguration, MAs provide additional spatial degrees of freedom to significantly boost beamforming gain and interference suppression. Specifically, we investigate a novel dual-domain security paradigm where networked base stations collaboratively protect uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmissions from communication eavesdropping while simultaneously safeguarding target sensing data against sensing eavesdroppers (SEs). To this end, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the sum of secrecy rates, subject to sensing requirements, SE eavesdropping probability constraint, and practical MA deployment constraints, by jointly optimizing receive combiners, transmit beamformers, UL power allocation, and MA positions. To address this non-convex problem with highly coupled variables, an efficient alternating optimization algorithm is proposed, integrating closed-form solutions for receive combiners, successive convex approximation for transmit beamforming and UL power, and a tailored sensing-aware multi-candidate particle swarm optimization for the high-dimensional MA positioning. Extensive numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, demonstrating that the proposed MA-enabled networked cooperative ISAC design significantly outperforms conventional fixed-position antenna-based designs in terms of security performance, while achieving notable power- and antenna-saving gains.

title: Performance Analysis of Discrete-Activation Pinching-Antenna Systems
summary: This paper investigates discrete-activation pinching antenna (DAPA) systems, where a finite set of pinching antennas (PAs) is deployed along a dielectric waveguide, from which PAs are selectively activated to serve users. Performance analyses are developed for both orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by explicitly accounting for the system geometry and discrete PA activation. Specifically, analytical expressions for the outage probability (OP) and ergodic rate (ER) are derived. Furthermore, the discrete-to-continuous gain ratio (DCGR) is introduced to quantify the normalized ER gain of a finite PA deployment relative to the single-PA and continuous-activation references. Monte Carlo simulations validate the derived expressions and show that DAPA systems can closely approach continuous-activation performance with only a moderate number of candidate PAs. For example, under the considered setup, DAPA with five PAs recovers approximately 92% and 90% of the continuous-activation ER gain under OMA and NOMA, respectively, at a transmit power of 0 dBm.

title: Passive Smartphone-Microphone Phonocardiography for Joint Maternal-Fetal Cardiac Well-Being Monitoring: A Longitudinal Self-Recorded Case Study in Late Pregnancy
comments: 11 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables, submitted to an IEEE venue for possible publication
summary: Maternal and perinatal deaths are concentrated in low- and middle-income countries, where routine fetal monitoring is largely inaccessible. With the prevalence of smartphone as personal assistive gadget, we ask whether a phone's built-in microphone, with no extra hardware or emitted signal, can serve as a software-only maternal-fetal cardiac screening aid when moved from the chest to the lower abdomen? We report a longitudinal, self-recorded case study of a single subject (Z) over the last five weeks of a singleton pregnancy, later delivered at term without complications: 28 short, uncontrolled recordings (rest, morning, post-exercise). Lacking maternal/fetal ground truth, we exploit the prior that maternal and fetal heart rates occupy largely disjoint frequency bands, blindly decomposing a Shannon-energy envelope into two candidate-rate bands, and additionally probe a slower breathing-rate band as a rest/exercise discriminator. A fast, regular, fetal-plausible rhythm was recovered from most recordings and remained essentially unchanged across maternal activity states, consistent with normal fetal cardiac autonomy; a slower, noisier maternal-plausible rhythm was recovered less reliably. Beat-to-beat variability proved largely noise-dominated at our short window lengths, and the breathing-rate probe did not significantly separate rest from exercise; both are reported as negative findings. We position the work within AI for global health: a low-cost screening aid for remote and underserved communities, pending reference-validated follow-up, not a replacement for clinical monitoring.
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables, submitted to an IEEE venue for possible publication

title: Exploiting Beam Squint for Near-Field Wideband Beamforming in Multi-User OFDMA Systems
summary: The beam squint effect has traditionally been viewed as detrimental to near-field wideband beamforming due to the reduction of beamforming gain towards the desired direction. In this paper, we show that it can instead be harnessed as a benefit in a hardware-constrained orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) system, where the system, equipped with a single radio-frequency (RF) chain, aims to serve multiple spatially distributed users by allocating different subcarriers to different users. By exploiting the beam squint effect, flexible frequency-dependent beamfocusing patterns are realized via parallel true-time-delay (TTD) units, enabling nearly full beamforming gain across users. In particular, we formulate a max-min rate optimization problem that jointly designs the time delays, subcarrier-user association, analog beamforming, and power allocation. To tackle the resulting nonconvex mixed-integer problem, a two-stage optimization framework is proposed. In Stage~I, subcarrier-user association and structured analog beamforming are jointly optimized. In Stage~II, power allocation is obtained via bisection search and inverse water-filling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve a significant improvement by utilizing beam squint to serve multiple spatially distributed users in OFDMA systems.

title: Widely Linear-Enhanced IQ Imbalance Interference Cancellation for AFDM-FTN Systems
summary: Internet of Things (IoT) networks require reliable and spectrally efficient wireless links to support massive device connectivity and high mobility applications. To meet these requirements, this paper investigates a widely linear (WL)-empowered receiver design for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) with faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling under practical receiver in phase and quadrature imbalance (IQI). The considered AFDM-FTN system couples the direct and image branches with FTN induced intersymbol interference (FTN-ISI) and delay-Doppler spreading in the affine domain. To address this coupled interference structure, a unified conjugate augmented input output model is established for IQI impaired AFDM-FTN systems. Based on this model, a WL minimum mean square error receiver with parallel interference cancellation (WL-MMSE-PIC) is developed, where WL-MMSE preprocessing is followed by the proposed hard decision PIC (HD-PIC) and damped soft decision PIC (SD-PIC). The proposed receiver is further analyzed in terms of the local stability of HD-PIC, a genie aided performance reference under ideal residual interference cancellation, and the impact of the AFDM chirp parameter on the post equalization interference distribution. Simulation results show that the proposed WL-MMSE-HD-PIC and WL-MMSE-SD-PIC receivers achieve significant error rate performance gains over the conventional linear-MMSE and WL-MMSE baselines. The results further show that FTN signaling provides a nominal spectral-efficiency gain, while residual-coupling-based chirp-parameter selection reduces the post-equalization residual coupling and improves detection reliability for high-mobility IoT links.

title: Target Sensing in Full-Dimensional MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems Via Coupled Tensor Decomposition
summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a key enabler for future wireless communication systems. However, existing ISAC designs based on MIMO-OFDM generally fail to fully exploit the spatial degrees of freedom and the communication data payload, resulting in restricted target sensing performance. To cope with this issue, in this paper we propose a novel target sensing method for full-dimensional (FD) MIMO-OFDM ISAC systems based on coupled tensor decomposition. We first characterize the system model of FD MIMO-OFDM ISAC, where the base station employs a large number of antennas in two dimensions and facilitates both sensing and communication via the data payload of OFDM signals. Then, we formulate the problem of estimating target parameters as a coupled canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) problem, which jointly leverages the echo signals of communication data payload over multiple subcarriers in the frequency domain. The theoretical analysis indicates that the formulated coupled CPD problem possesses a more relaxed uniqueness condition compared with the ordinary CPD problem, thereby enabling more stable target sensing performance through the pure communication data payload in FD MIMO-OFDM ISAC. In addition, we develop a coupled CPD-based target sensing algorithm, where the target parameters, including azimuth and elevation angles, ranges, and velocities, are extracted from the decomposed factor matrices. Numerical results show that the proposed target sensing method achieves a higher success rate and more accurate parameter estimation than existing tensor decomposition methods.

title: SpikeAid: A Streaming Spiking Hearing Aid Framework for Joint Noise Reduction and Wide Dynamic Range Compression
summary: Modern hearing aids combine noise reduction (NR) with wide dynamic range compression (WDRC) to suppress background interference while compensating for the reduced auditory dynamic range associated with hearing loss. Conventional systems typically process NR and WDRC as separate stages, although the output of NR directly affects the signal levels and envelopes that determine subsequent compression. Recent end-to-end neural approaches can jointly optimize these processes, but their dense computation remains challenging for always-on hearing aids. In this work, we propose SpikeAid, a causal end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) framework for joint NR and WDRC. SpikeAid consists of an NR-Net that constructs complementary speech and noise representations and a WDRC-Net that estimates the corresponding branch gains, with both components jointly optimized according to the final hearing aid objective. To capture the multiscale temporal structures required by joint NR and WDRC in a computationally efficient manner, we further introduce the Delayed Resonate-and-fire Neuron (DRN), which incorporates bio-inspired heterogeneous dendritic delays and resonating dynamics. Experimental results on the hearing aid task show that SpikeAid improves key objective metrics over cascaded processing and outperforms existing spiking speech-processing baselines. Evaluation on the public Intel Neuromorphic Deep Noise Suppression (N-DNS) Challenge further demonstrates state-of-the-art neuromorphic speech-denoising performance with DRN. Finally, we designed an FPGA-based neuromorphic hardware system for efficient deployment of SpikeAid, where it achieves over two orders of magnitude higher energy efficiency than conventional CPU/GPU implementations, demonstrating its potential for energy-efficient hearing aid applications.

title: A Mathematical Framework for EEG Functional Connectivity: Taxonomy, Measure Relationships, Identifiability, and Analytical Bounds
summary: Electroencephalographic (EEG) functional connectivity is quantified using diverse measures of statistical dependence, spectral coupling, phase synchronization, information transfer, directed interactions, cross-frequency coupling, and network topology. An important question is what can be inferred about one connectivity measure from another. This paper develops a mathematical framework that treats connectivity measures as mappings from an explicitly defined admissible state space to observable values. For a source measure and a target measure, the set of target values compatible with an observed source value is defined as a cross-connectivity attainable set. This formulation distinguishes exact determination, conditional determination using additional information, bounded inference, approximate identification, and non-identifiability. The framework is extended to multichannel connectivity matrices, graph measures, and dynamic connectivity. It also incorporates the influence of filtering, referencing, volume conduction, source leakage, inverse modeling, epoch duration, and estimator assumptions on admissible inferences. Analytical examples examine relationships between covariance and correlation, mutual information and correlation under joint Gaussianity, coherence and phase-locking value under restrictive signal conditions, and the general non-identifiability of the phase-lag index and weighted phase-lag index without additional assumptions. By making assumptions and attainable values explicit, the framework provides a systematic basis for determining what connectivity results can and cannot establish about other measures.

title: Joint Probabilistic Shaping and Symbol-Level Precoding for Covert LEO Satellite Downlinks
summary: The wide footprint of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks exposes the mere occurrence of a transmission to any receiver within it. This paper studies covert multiuser LEO downlinks, where a passive warden at an unknown but fixed ground location accumulates observations as the satellite moves. We jointly optimize the precoding and the occurrence probabilities of the multiuser symbol combinations to provide covertness against such wardens. Each phase-shift keying (PSK) symbol vector is decomposed into a relative pattern and a common rotation, so that shaping the pattern probabilities leaves the symbols of every legitimate user uniformly distributed. We develop probabilistically shaped symbol-level precoding and probabilistically shaped block-level precoding. We derive the exact chi-square divergence of the warden's Gaussian-mixture observation over the complete session and, by bounding the leakage over a continuous location uncertainty region, obtain certificates that guarantee covertness throughout that region. The certified covertness level is minimized under robust constructive-interference, power, and entropy constraints through an alternating optimization whose updates are equivalent to convex conic problems, and the optimized probabilities follow a Maxwell--Boltzmann-type law. Numerical results show that shaping substantially reduces the certified covertness level of both precoding structures, particularly under large location uncertainty, low elevation, and scarce power.

title: A Novel OFDM-FMCW Waveform for Low-Complexity Joint Sensing and Communication
summary: With the advent of 6th Generation (6G) wireless networks, integrating Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) waveforms presents a promising solution for simultaneous communication and sensing. While OFDM offers high communication performance, it requires complex transceivers for sensing applications. Conversely, FMCW is easily implemented for sensing but provides low data rates for communication. This letter derives the mathematical relationship between OFDM and FMCW, showing how FMCW can be generated from the diagonal elements of the OFDM modulator (\ie, the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) matrix). We propose a novel approach that leverages the DFT matrix to seamlessly integrate these two waveforms, minimizing interference and enabling high data rate communication alongside low-complexity sensing receiver design. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique in achieving simultaneous sensing and

title: Secure Distortion-Aware GNN Precoding under Active Eavesdropping in Cell-Free Networks
summary: This paper considers a cell-free (CF) network under active eavesdropping. We show that nonlinear power amplifier (PA) distortion, together with the per-access point (AP) large-scale-gain fingerprint of the attack, can be exploited across cooperating APs to enhance physical layer security (PLS). Classical zero-forcing (ZF)-artificial noise (AN) precoders rely on a linear transmitter and an unbiased estimate, and thus cannot exploit either. We propose a distortion aware graph neural network (GNN) precoder that designs the signal beams at cooperating APs and exploits both the PA distortion and the per-AP fingerprint to enhance the secrecy rate, combined with a null-space AN block to form the GNN-AN scheme. The GNN is trained on channel estimates biased by an uplink pilot-spoofing attack to maximise the average per-user secrecy rate. Simulations across different numbers of APs show uniformly higher outage secrecy rates than ZF-AN under attack, reaching gains of 15% at the 1% outage level and 8.9% at the 5% outage level at L = 32 APs, input back-off (IBO) = -1 dB, and attacker-to-targeted user pilot power ratio of 0.5, under the same signal/AN power split.

title: Receiver Design for Continuous-Time AFDM based on Pre-Filter De-Chirp
comments: Submitted to IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC 2027)
summary: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising waveform for future high-mobility communications due to its Doppler robustness and diversity gain. However, existing continuous-time AFDM relies on chirp-dependent wideband receive filtering, which increases noise power and causes channel-energy leakage. In this paper, we propose an AFDM reception scheme based on pre-filter de-chirp for doubly selective channels. The coupling between de-chirp and the channel is first characterized, yielding an equivalent path representation with delay-coupled effective Doppler shifts. The discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT)-domain equivalent channel is then derived under general transmit pulse shaping and linear time-invariant receive filtering, showing that the effective filtering kernel depends only on the relative sample offset and avoids the additional spreading caused by conventional chirp-dependent filtering. The receive-noise power is further analyzed, and an explicit expression for the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gap is obtained by the required receive-filter bandwidths. Simulations verify the theoretical SNR analysis and show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the conventional scheme while approaching ideal discrete-time AFDM.
comment: Submitted to IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC 2027)

title: Learning Speaker-Activity-Conditioned WavLM Speaker Embeddings with Real Conversational Data
summary: End-to-end neural diarization with vector clustering (EEND-VC) is a strong framework for long-form conversational diarization, where speaker embeddings are used to link local speaker decisions across windows. Conventional EEND-VC systems extract these embeddings by cutting out regions assigned to each local speaker, preferably using only non-overlapped speech. This works well when enough clean target-speaker speech is available, but it discards useful speaker evidence in overlapped regions and becomes unreliable when a local speaker appears mostly in overlap. We propose a speaker-activity-conditioned embedding extractor that adapts a pretrained WavLM-MHFA speaker verification model to extract target-speaker embeddings directly from full conversational windows. Inspired by the recently proposed diarization-conditioned Whisper (DiCoW) model for target-speaker ASR, frame-level diarization-dependent transformations inject local speaker-activity information into intermediate WavLM representations while preserving the pretrained initialization. Experiments on multiple conversational diarization benchmarks show that fine-tuning with limited real meeting data reduces speaker-confusion errors and improves EEND-VC diarization performance. The results further indicate that real conversational data provides an effective alternative to large-scale simulated-mixture training for diarization-aware speaker embedding extraction.

title: Image Restoration with Impulse Noise Based on Minimax Concave Penalty: Grayscale and Color Images
summary: In today's world-where social networks play a significant role-images serve as one of the most important tools for transferring concepts. Image degradation caused by noise or blurring hinders the effective transmission of the information we expect to derive from an image. Consequently, developing image restoration methods capable of revealing crucial information is of great importance. In this work, a model for impulse noise image restoring is proposed by using a Minimax Concave Penalty. The proposed model is applicable to both color and grayscale images. Then, a numerical algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers is introduced, and the convergence of the method is analyzed both theoretically and numerically. In the final step, the proposed method is evaluated through simulations on several examples, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness.

title: Probing and Mitigating Hallucinations in Speech-augmented Language Models for Automatic Speech Recognition via Small Language Models
summary: The widespread success of large language models in natural language processing has spurred the development of speech-augmented language models (SLMs) to extend their reasoning capabilities from textual inputs to spoken ones. Despite impressive performance, SLMs remain susceptible to hallucinations, posing challenges in practical utility. To this end, we first probe hallucinations in SLMs for automatic speech recognition (ASR) via the lens of causal mediation and behavioral analysis. To mitigate fabricated ASR hypotheses, we propose AudioSLM, a compact yet effective ASR framework built upon a small language model, which leverages alignment cues and cross-attention layers to synergistically bolster acoustic modeling and cross-modal interactions. Experiments on LibriSpeech reveal that hallucinations arise from multi-head self-attention modules with an excessive attention bias towards textual tokens. AudioSLM considerably eases ASR hallucinations and outperforms some LLM-based ASR models.

title: Low-Dimensional Hermite-Gaussian Representations for Ptychographic Reconstruction
summary: We analyze the reconstruction error of a low-dimensional Hermite--Gaussian (HG) ptychographic method used in real-time Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD) reconstruction. We derive an upper bound on the discrepancy between the low-dimensional, aberration-corrected reconstruction and classical Fourier-domain WDD. The bound decomposes the reconstruction error into contributions from HG--Fourier basis mismatch and aberration-coefficient mismatch, explicitly characterizing their dependence on the number of retained HG modes, Wiener regularization, aberration mismatch, and measurement dose. Numerical experiments on simulated electron and X-ray ptychographic data characterize these dependencies and demonstrate robustness to Poisson noise. These results provide theoretical and guidance for selecting the reduced representation and reconstruction parameters, enabling computationally and memory-efficient for near-real-time ptychographic reconstruction.

title: On the Optimal Power Allocation and Performance Analysis for the HSIC-PA Aided Hybrid NOMA
summary: Hybrid non-orthogonal multiple access (H-NOMA), which leverages the complementary advantages of orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and NOMA, has emerged as a promising technique for next-generation wireless networks. This paper investigates power allocation optimization for the OMA and NOMA time slots allocated to the opportunistic user in H-NOMA systems, aiming to overcome the limitations of conventional equal power allocation strategies. Specifically, we consider an H-NOMA scheme that integrates hybrid successive interference cancellation (HSIC) with power adaptation (PA), referred to as the HSIC-PA aided H-NOMA scheme. To better adapt to practical communication scenarios, distinct power coefficients are assigned to the OMA and NOMA time slots of the opportunistic user to maximize the achievable data rate. Closed-form expressions for the optimal power allocation coefficients are derived, and simulation results validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the theoretical analysis.

title: PronCFT: Pronunciation Contextual Fine-Tuning for Contextual Biasing of Out-of-Vocabulary Words in LLM-Based ASR
summary: LLM-based ASR systems often replace rare and out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words with familiar words that sound similar. Two factors contribute to this error: the model has not learned how an unseen word's sound maps to its spelling, and it may favor a familiar word over the one spoken, a failure we call prior suppression. Providing candidate pronunciations alone may not help: the model can treat a phoneme annotation as a marker that raises a candidate's output probability without checking its pronunciation against the speech. We propose PronCFT, which uses fixed phoneme sequences and trains the model to transcribe speech into phonemes, match them to context candidates, and output the matched spelling. During training, we alter candidate spellings while keeping their pronunciations unchanged, discouraging the model from choosing a familiar spelling without checking how the candidate sounds. A curriculum then gradually removes intermediate outputs to reduce decoding latency and prevent phoneme transcription errors from affecting the final text. The model's retained ability to use pronunciation cues suggests that this ability can be internalized. On an OOV test set filtered from open-source benchmarks, the final model, PronCFT-C, significantly improves recall from 59.89% to 83.57% (+23.68 pp). Wrong-phoneme and spelling-interference tests indicate that the gain depends on phoneme content rather than the presence of an annotation.

title: Image CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction for Image Communication
summary: Semantic error correction (SEC) uses the semantic knowledge of pretrained models to complement conventional channel decoding. By combining physical-layer decoding information with application-layer semantic predictions, cross-layer SEC (CL-SEC) has demonstrated substantial performance gains in text transmission; however, its applicability to image transmission remains largely unexplored. This paper proposes Image CL-SEC, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first extension of the CL-SEC framework to image transmission. Image CL-SEC uses channel-decoding information together with contextual predictions from a pretrained visual model to resolve residual uncertainty after forward error correction (FEC) decoding. In our implementation, images are represented as discrete visual tokens. For each token position selected for re-evaluation, the probability distribution produced by the channel decoder is combined with the distribution predicted by the visual model to identify the most likely transmitted token. The resulting decision therefore reflects both channel evidence and visual context. Experiments across multiple channel conditions show that, at low and moderate signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), Image CL-SEC improves pixel-level fidelity, perceptual similarity, and token-recovery accuracy relative to either channel decoding or visual-model inference alone. Supplementary experiments using different pretrained visual models further demonstrate that these gains are not specific to a single model.

title: MS-Bench: A Condition-Stratified Multi-Speaker ASR Benchmark
summary: Multi-speaker automatic speech recognition (MSASR) has advanced rapidly with end-to-end speech large language models. However, existing benchmarks cover limited ranges of specific multi-speaker conditions and scenarios, making it difficult to reveal system limitations under diverse conditions and scenarios. We introduce MS-Bench\footnote{\href{https://aslp-lab.github.io/MS-Bench/}{Demo page: https://aslp-lab.github.io/MS-Bench/}}, a condition-stratified benchmark for fine-grained MSASR evaluation. MS-Bench integrates both public and internal benchmarks and characterizes each recording along five dimensions: speaker number, overlap ratio, speaker similarity, speaker turn interval, and acoustic quality. We stratify these dimensions into condition ranges and construct MS-Bench with broad coverage of conditions, scenarios, languages, and recording devices. Evaluating representative commercial, open-source, and cascaded systems, we find that overlap affects both lexical recognition and speaker attribution, while other factors exhibit more task-specific effects on recognition, attribution, or temporal prediction. These results demonstrate that aggregate metrics alone obscure important MSASR failure modes and highlight the value of condition-stratified evaluation. MS-Bench aims to reveal condition-specific limitations of current MSASR systems and guide future improvements.

title: One-Bit Coherent Distributed Radar Detection in Clutter via Velocity-Plane Search: Vanishing Loss and EEC-Calibrated Thresholding
summary: Coherent distributed radar architectures enhance the detectability of low-reflectivity targets. However, conventional coherent processing generally entails prohibitively large volumes of inter-station data exchange, thereby motivating the adoption of one-bit quantization strategies. In this work, we investigate a clutter-dominated regime in which the interference is driven by a dense ensemble of weak scatterers. We demonstrate that, under these conditions, one-bit quantization can exhibit a vanishing performance loss with respect to ideal high-resolution sampling in terms of detection capability, in contrast to the classical 2 dB performance penalty associated with one-bit detection in white Gaussian noise environments. For unknown target velocity, we reformulate joint velocity-search processing under the effective one-bit model. Maximizing over the velocity plane makes false-alarm calibration an extreme-value problem for a correlated two-dimensional random field, whose maximum is not characterized by its pointwise null distribution alone. We therefore use an expected Euler characteristic approximation to calibrate the search threshold. We obtain analytic expressions for a separable two-station geometry and use constrained coefficient fitting for larger networks. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate negligible quantization loss in the clutter-dominated setting and conservative false-alarm calibration under the tested Gaussian slow-time model.

title: Learnable Pilot Design for OFDM-based Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding
comments: Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)
summary: Recent advances in deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) have shown strong robustness to channel variations in wireless image transmission. However, its integration with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) typically relies on fixed pilot patterns that are not optimized for receiver- side channel processing. This work introduces Pilot-Efficient DeepJSCC-OFDM (PE-JSCC), which learns pilot placement under a strictly fixed number of pilot symbols via a Gumbel- Top-k-based selector. The learned pilot placement improves end- to-end performance over the conventional Block-JSCC, Comb- JSCC, and Scatter-JSCC baselines. To support high mobility, the receiver incorporates a lightweight axial-attention-based inter- carrier interference (ICI) canceler and a CNN-based channel estimator. Simulation results show that PE-JSCC consistently outperforms fixed pilot patterns across diverse SNRs and remains robust over a wide mobility range.
comment: Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)

title: Optical ISAC with Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) Arrays
summary: Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays offer photon-level sensitivity for sensing in optical integrated sensing and communication (O-ISAC). However, after each detection, a SPAD is blind for a dead time, which saturates the array at high received power. Existing O-ISAC analyses assume linear receivers and do not capture this effect. In this paper, we study ranging with a SPAD array in a monostatic O-ISAC system based on direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM). Sampling the array once per dead time, we model the number of pixels that detect a photon in each sampling interval as a binomial random variable whose success probability accounts for the intensity variation of the echo within a dead time. Based on this model, we derive the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for range estimation. We show that the SPAD count model of optical wireless communication, which assumes a constant photon rate over a dead time, causes a range bias that depends on the received power. Moreover, unlike for a linear photodiode, saturation degrades the ranging accuracy beyond a sensing-optimal transmit power. The rate-constrained operating point is then the larger of this power and the power needed for the target data rate. Numerical results validate the analysis against a continuous-time photon-counting simulation and show that the proposed model is needed for ranging.

title: Localization Gains from Explanation Regularization Should Not Be Interpreted as Faithfulness Gains.
summary: Training-time explanation regularization is often evaluated by whether saliency maps become more concentrated within annotated regions. We argue that this criterion alone is insufficient: transformation consistency, lesion localization, and faithfulness to the classifier are distinct properties and should be evaluated separately, particularly in medical imaging. We examine this distinction through a case study of Contrastive Grad-CAM Consistency (CGC) in three-class brain tumor MRI classification. Using a single-channel ResNet-50 with five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation, we compare a cross-entropy baseline with CGC. CGC changes overall Pointing Game (PG) from $27.24\%$ to $36.02\%$ and Relevance Mass Accuracy (RMA) from $11.17\%$ to $18.01\%$, while classification accuracy changes from $93.63\%$ to $94.87\%$. Perturbation-based faithfulness metrics show inconsistent changes: Insertion Area Under the Curve (IAUC) changes from $0.73$ to $0.78$, whereas Deletion Area Under the Curve (DAUC) favors the baseline ($0.36$ versus $0.41$; lower is better), and overall Iterative Removal Of Features (IROF) is $0.57$ for both models. These results support our position that improved spatial agreement with pathology should not be interpreted as a general improvement in explanation faithfulness. We therefore recommend property-specific evaluation in which the property targeted by the explanation objective, spatial agreement with reference regions, and model reliance are measured and reported separately.

title: On the Performance of RIS Transmitter with Receive Combining Techniques
summary: In this paper, we investigate the impact of practical phase-shift constraint of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) on multi-antenna systems employing maximal ratio combining (MRC) and receive antenna selection (RAS). Since each element of RIS can apply only a single phase-shift at a given time, the system performance degrades substantially when multiple receive antennas are active simultaneously. To quantify this effect, closed-form outage probability expressions are derived and asymptotic analyses are carried out over Rician fading channels. We show that the practical phase-shift constraint of RIS degrades the diversity order of MRC and in addition, RAS outperforms MRC, contrary to the conventional performance ordering of these techniques.

title: Signal Design Impacts on GNSS and LEO-PNT L1 Band Acquisition Complexity: A Case Study with Xona Pulsar
summary:
GNSS signal acquisition is the process of detecting and estimating signal parameters by exploiting correlation operations that provide processing gain and enable the detection of signals below the noise floor. The design of an acquisition engine requires balancing achievable sensitivity, computational complexity, memory requirements, power consumption, and implementation complexity. In particular, increasing coherent and non-coherent integration times improves sensitivity but can significantly increase receiver processing requirements, limiting its applicability in low-power and resource-constrained receivers.
  This paper presents a comparative analysis of L1-band signal acquisition complexity by evaluating the required integration time and corresponding implementation requirements for different signal designs under equivalent acquisition performance targets. The analysis considers the impact of signal characteristics, including spreading codes, secondary codes, modulation, and signal bandwidth, on coherent and non-coherent acquisition performance. For a given attenuation level and target probability of false alarm and detection, the required integration times are derived and translated into acquisition complexity metrics, including arithmetic operations, processing time, and memory requirements.
  The analysis is applied to Pulsar X1, a LEO-enabled PNT signal, and representative GNSS L1 signals to determine under which attenuation, assistance, and integration conditions the higher received power of LEO-PNT translates into reduced receiver acquisition workload. By relating the required integration to arithmetic operations, processing time, and memory requirements, the study provides a receiver-level comparison relevant to both conventional and snapshot-based receivers, where reducing acquisition processing can directly contribute to lower energy consumption.

title: Does Synchrophasor Attenuation Preclude Detection of High-Frequency Oscillations?
summary: Recent work suggests that standard synchrophasors are inadequate for capturing high-frequency data center oscillations, primarily due to filtering and windowing attenuation during phasor estimation. We prove that widely used periodogram and RMS energy detectors remain largely robust to it and confirm this by simulation.

title: Vision--RF Cooperative ISAC for Dynamic V2I Networks: Adaptive Beam Management and Semantic Clutter Suppression
summary: We develop a vision--radio-frequency (RF) cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that jointly uses visual priors and RF observations for transmit-side beam control and receiver-side clutter suppression. Within a narrowband snapshot model, visual target priors and historical RF detections guide control in dynamic vehicle-to-infrastructure networks with roadside clutter. In this framework, posterior angular uncertainty determines beam control and the selection between communication-for-sensing and sensing-for-sensing modes. To reduce sensing overhead while accommodating unreliable visual information, we develop a reliability-adaptive beam scanning scheme that allocates a bounded scan budget according to visual target probabilities and RF history, while reserving an adaptive fraction for exploration. At the receiver, visual geometry identifies clutter support, and RF observations estimate the corresponding complex reflection coefficients. Motion-aware residual filtering is then applied before angle--Doppler detection to suppress clutter while preserving slow-moving targets. Furthermore, communication and sensing power allocation is formulated as a per-direction linear program, subject to signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio constraints evaluated at angles sampled from the posterior distribution and a total-power budget. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves tracking over static and vision-only beam control and reduces sensing overhead relative to full scanning. The proposed scanning scheme also provides greater robustness to visual blockage than fixed-weight scanning, while the receiver better preserves slow-moving targets than temporal cancellation when visual target information is available.

title: From Data to Deployment: A Scoping Review of Empirical Tools, Techniques, and Operational Readiness in Data-Driven 5G/6G Network Optimization
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to 5G/6G network optimization, yet differences in empirical evidence, evaluation methods, and computational requirements complicate comparisons of reported performance. This scop ing review synthesizes 72 peer-reviewed journal studies pub lished between 2022 and 2026, selected through a PRISMA ScR-informed process from 893 records. The review examines empirical tools, AI/ML techniques, optimization domains, and operational readiness. Evidence classification identifies 37 studies (51.4%) using real-world or physical-testbed evidence only, 25 (34.7%) combining measured and simulated evidence, and 10 (13.9%) relying exclusively on synthetic or simulated data. Offline analysis was the most common evaluation setting, accounting for 45 studies (62.5%). Three principal findings emerge. First, empirical measurements improve contextual relevance, while simulation and digital twins support scalable experimentation but introduce validation challenges. Second, algorithmic effectiveness depends on the optimization objective, data characteristics, and computational constraints rather than model complexity alone. Third, predictive accuracy is more consistently evaluated than the network-level effects of optimization decisions. The review there fore introduces the six-module Evidence Fidelity and Operational Reporting (EFOR) checklist to improve evaluation consistency, reporting transparency, and operational relevance.

title: Doppler-compensated Space-time Coding for MIMO PMCW Radar
comments: Under review for a publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing
summary: Phase modulated continuous wave (PMCW) radar is an attractive choice for automotive sensing due to its high dynamic range, interference robustness, and support for integrated communication and sensing. In multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) PMCW radar, code division multiplexing (CDM) separates transmit signals, but non-ideal auto- and cross-correlation properties increase range sidelobes and degrade dynamic range. This paper proposes a Doppler-compensated space-time coding (STC)-based MIMO PMCW radar framework that separates transmit signals before range correlation, eliminating cross-correlation terms under perfect compensation and allowing the same binary sequence to be used across transmit antennas. The Doppler influence on STC decoding is analytically characterized, showing that chip-wise and inter-STC-slot phase distortions increase range sidelobes and generate ghost components in the direction-of-arrival (DOA) spectrum. To mitigate these effects, Doppler is estimated first, followed by joint fast-time and STC-slot compensation before decoding. Residual STC leakage under imperfect Doppler estimation is quantified, and the processing is extended to multiple moving targets through Doppler-bin-dependent compensation. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate reduced range sidelobes and suppression of DOA ghosts, while maintaining flexibility in code sequence design.
comment: Under review for a publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing

title: Causal adaptive intensity estimation for non-stationary point processes: a Kalman-kernel duality framework
summary: Estimating the instantaneous conditional intensity of a non-stationary point process from a single realization of discrete event timestamps is a fundamental problem in computational neuroscience, quantitative finance, and network monitoring. Traditional adaptive kernel methods achieve variable bandwidths through Abramson's square-root law, yet existing implementations require non-causal access to the complete event record and incur $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ or at best $\mathcal{O}(N \log N)$ computational cost. Causal alternatives based on reciprocal inter-arrival times, meanwhile, suffer from systematic divergence under Poisson and bursty arrival dynamics due to Jensen's inequality. This paper addresses both limitations by establishing a formal duality between steady-state Kalman filtering and adaptive exponential kernel smoothing. An endogenous state-space observer is constructed in which Poisson counting statistics dictate the measurement noise ($R \propto λ$) and geometric diffusion governs the process volatility ($Q \propto λ^2$). Under these physically motivated axioms, the algebraic Riccati equation autonomously yields an effective smoothing bandwidth scaling as $τ\propto λ^{-1/2}$, giving a causal, recursive, $\mathcal{O}(1)$ per-step realization of square-root adaptive bandwidth scaling. A second-order constant-velocity extension produces a $λ^{-1/4}$ scaling that reduces approximation bias, and a probabilistic dormant-state gating mechanism suppresses phantom intensity leakage during structural zeros. Synthetic benchmarks together with neural and financial data show that the observer adapts across orders of magnitude in intensity with an empirical per-step cost of approximately 30\,$μ$s.

title: Sensitivity and Identifiability of Tumor-Related Changes in Longitudinal Microwave Breast Imaging
summary: Microwave imaging could monitor breast tumor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but between-visit changes in breast positioning and normal tissue may confound tumor-related changes. We use eight patient-specific dielectric models from longitudinal MRI of two patients at four time points. For each model, 24-port S-parameters were simulated from 1 to 3 GHz, and Jacobians computed for tumor permittivity and loss, fibroglandular tissue (FGT) permittivity, and breast rotation and translation. 1 mm positioning changes produced changes 20 to 50 times larger than a 10% tumor permittivity change above 2 GHz. Nevertheless, tumor sensitivity patterns were weakly aligned with positioning patterns, tumor-FGT similarity exceeded 0.8 at only some visits, and the Jacobians remained well conditioned. Tumor responses are thus small but separable; monitoring will require positioning correction, frequency selection, and noise-aware detectability analysis.

title: Evidence for Phenotype-Driven Disparities in Freezing of Gait Detection and Approaches to Bias Mitigation
comments: Revised manuscript for EJN Special Issue Submission
summary: Freezing of gait (FOG) is a debilitating feature of Parkinson's disease (PD) and a common cause of injurious falls. Recent advances in wearable-based human activity recognition (HAR) have enabled FOG detection, but bias and fairness in these models remain understudied. Bias is defined as a systematic error leading to unequal outcomes, while fairness refers to consistent performance across subject groups. Biased models could systematically underserve patients with specific FOG phenotypes or demographics, widening care disparities. We evaluated the bias and fairness of state-of-the-art HAR models for FOG detection across FOG phenotypes and patient demographics using 4 public wearable datasets (145 subjects and 59.8 hours of recording) with multiple on-body sensor locations and temporal annotations on FOG episodes across various behavioral test protocols. Four mitigation approaches were assessed: conventional methods (threshold optimization and adversarial debiasing) and two transfer learning-based approaches (multi-site transfer and fine-tuning pre-trained models). Fairness was primarily quantified using the demographic parity ratio (DPR) and the equalized odds ratio (EOR). HAR models exhibited substantial bias (DPR & EOR < 0.8) across age, sex, disease duration, and critically, FOG phenotype. This phenotype-specific bias is particularly concerning as tremulous and akinetic FOG may require different clinical management. Conventional methods failed: threshold optimization (DPR=-0.126, EOR=+0.063) and adversarial debiasing (DPR=-0.008, EOR=-0.001). In contrast, multi-site transfer learning improved fairness (DPR=+0.037, p<0.01; EOR=+0.045, p<0.01) and performance (F1-score=+0.020, p<0.05), though neither metric reached 0.8. Transfer learning across diverse datasets may partially mitigate these disparities, helping wearable-based FOG monitoring benefit all individuals with PD.
comment: Revised manuscript for EJN Special Issue Submission

title: Revisiting Beamforming Design for Stable Millimeter-Wave Communications Under Blockages
comments: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: This paper investigates robust analog beamforming for millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications under stochastic path blockages using multi-panel arrays. Conventional designs concentrate beams on the line-of-sight (LoS) path to maximize array gain, but this approach is highly vulnerable to sudden disconnections when the LoS path is blocked. To overcome this limitation, we propose a multi-beam design that exploits both LoS and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths for stable communications. The major contribution of this work is to establish a theoretical foundation for multi-beam design, where closed-form expressions for the cumulative distribution function (CDF) and outage probability of the spectral efficiency (SE) are derived. To design the optimal multi-beam based on the derived outage probability, we formulate a panel allocation problem to determine the assignment of panels to specific paths. The optimization problem can be solved by two algorithms based on brute-force search. Through computer simulations, the validity of the theoretical analysis for multi-beam design is confirmed, and the proposed algorithms substantially reduce the outage probability while maintaining average SE performance, thereby achieving stable communication.
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

title: OncoReg: Medical Image Registration for Oncological Challenges
comments: Accepted for publication at the Journal of Machine Learning for Biomedical Imaging (MELBA) https://melba-journal.org/2026:029
summary: In modern cancer research, the vast volume of medical data generated is often underutilised due to challenges related to patient privacy. The OncoReg Challenge addresses this issue by enabling researchers to develop and validate image registration methods through a two-phase framework that ensures patient privacy while fostering the development of more generalisable AI models. Phase one involves working with a publicly available dataset, while phase two focuses on training models on a private dataset within secure hospital networks. OncoReg builds upon the foundation established by the Learn2Reg Challenge by incorporating the registration of interventional cone-beam computed tomography with standard planning fan-beam CT images in radiotherapy. Accurate image registration is crucial in oncology, particularly for dynamic treatment adjustments in image-guided radiotherapy, where precise alignment is necessary to minimise radiation exposure to healthy tissues while effectively targeting tumours. This work details the methodology and data behind the OncoReg Challenge and provides a comprehensive analysis of the competition entries and results. Findings reveal that feature extraction plays a pivotal role in this registration task. A new method emerging from this challenge demonstrated its versatility, while established approaches continue to perform comparably to newer techniques. Both deep learning and classical approaches still play significant roles in image registration, with the combination of methods, particularly in feature extraction, proving most effective.
comment: Accepted for publication at the Journal of Machine Learning for Biomedical Imaging (MELBA) https://melba-journal.org/2026:029

title: Dynamically Slimmable Speech Enhancement Network with Metric-Guided Training
summary: To further reduce the complexity of lightweight speech enhancement models, we introduce a gating-based Dynamically Slimmable Network (DSN). The DSN comprises static and dynamic components. For architecture-independent applicability, we introduce distinct dynamic structures targeting the commonly used components, namely, grouped recurrent neural network units, multi-head attention, convolutional, and fully connected layers. A policy module adaptively governs the use of dynamic parts at a frame-wise resolution according to the input signal quality, controlling computational load. We further propose Metric-Guided Training (MGT) to explicitly guide the policy module in assessing input speech quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the DSN achieves comparable enhancement performance in instrumental metrics to the state-of-the-art lightweight baseline, while using only 73% of its computational load on average. Evaluations of dynamic component usage ratios indicate that the MGT-DSN can appropriately allocate network resources according to the severity of input signal distortion.

title: SLIM: Semantic-based Low-bitrate Image compression for Machines
summary: In recent years, the demand of image compression models for machine vision has increased dramatically. However, the training frameworks of image compression still focus on the vision of human, preserving unnecessary details and limiting bitrate efficiency for machine vision tasks. In this paper, we propose Semantic-based Low-bitrate Image compression for Machines, termed SLIM. This proposed framework consists of two key components: RoI-focused latent compression and semantic latent enhancement with dual cues. First, the latent compressor is trained to focus on Region-of-Interest (RoI) areas that are semantically and functionally important for machine vision tasks in the latent space, while requiring no explicit masks during inference. Second, to compensate for severe information loss at extremely low bitrates, a diffusion-based semantic decoder enhances the compressed latent with a pretrained diffusion model guided by two complementary cues provided by an RoI-focused latent and text-based semantic guidance. This design preserves RoI details that are critical for machine perception while maintaining semantically coherent and artifact-suppressed non-RoI regions under extremely low bitrates. Experimental results show that SLIM consistently achieves strong performance across diverse machine vision tasks under the same bits per pixel condition, compared to conventional image compression models for machines. Our code is available at https://github.com/mcml-official/SLIM

title: LEO Constellations as a Decentralized GNSS Network: Optimizing PNT Corrections in Space
comments: Accepted by IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
summary: With the rapid expansion of low Earth orbit (LEO) constellations, thousands of satellites are now in operation, many equipped with onboard GNSS receivers capable of continuous orbit determination and time synchronization. This development is creating an unprecedented spaceborne GNSS network, offering new opportunities for network-driven precise LEO orbit and clock estimation. Yet, current onboard GNSS processing is largely standalone and often insufficient for high-precision applications, while centralized fusion is challenging due to computational bottlenecks and the lack of in-orbit infrastructure. In this work, we report a decentralized GNSS network over large-scale LEO constellations, where each satellite processes its own measurements while exchanging compact information with neighboring nodes to enable precise orbit and time determination. We model the moving constellation as a dynamic graph and employ a momentum-accelerated gradient tracking (GT) method to achieve stable convergence despite topology changes. Numerical simulations with constellations containing hundreds of satellites show that the proposed method matches the accuracy of an ideal centralized benchmark. Ultimately, this framework supports the development of autonomous and self-organizing space systems, enabling high-precision navigation with reduced dependence on continuous ground contact.
comment: Accepted by IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications

title: Diagnostic Impact of Cine Clips for Thyroid Nodule Assessment on Ultrasound
comments: 26 pages, 7 tables. v2: intrareader agreement now compares the same nodule across rounds and is lower with cine images; deep-learning comparator results and between-round p-values (two-sided patient-level bootstrap) recomputed; table misprints corrected; ACR TI-RADS spongiform rule applied; kappa, multireader ROC and size-independent analyses and literature review added. Main finding unchanged
summary: Objective: Thyroid ultrasound is commonly performed using a combination of static images and cine clips (video recordings). However, the exact utility and impact of cine images remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of cine imaging on accuracy and consistency of thyroid nodule assessment, using the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging, Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS). Methods: 50 benign and 50 malignant thyroid nodules with cytopathology results, from 89 patients, were included. A reader study with 4 specialty-trained radiologists was then conducted over 3 rounds, assessing only static images in the first two rounds and both static and cine images in the third round. TI-RADS scores and the consequent management recommendations were then evaluated by comparing them to the malignancy status of the nodules. Results: Mean sensitivity for malignancy detection was 0.65 for static images and 0.67 with both static and cine images (p=0.41). Specificity was 0.20 for static images and 0.22 with both static and cine images (p=0.25). Management recommendations were similar with and without cine images. Intrareader agreement on feature assignments was slightly lower when cine images were added (0.83 vs 0.87, p<0.001), and TI-RADS point totals changed more between rounds with cine images. Conclusion: The inclusion of cine imaging for thyroid nodule assessment on ultrasound did not significantly change diagnostic performance in this reader study, although it changed some feature assignments. Current practice guidelines, which do not mandate cine imaging, may be sufficient for TI-RADS-based management recommendations.

title: RF-GPT: Teaching AI to See the Wireless World
summary: Large language models (LLMs) and multimodal models have become powerful general-purpose reasoning systems. However, radio-frequency (RF) signals, which underpin wireless systems, are still not natively supported by these models. Existing LLM-based approaches for telecom focus mainly on text and structured data, while conventional RF deep-learning models are built separately for specific signal-processing tasks, highlighting a clear gap between RF perception and high-level reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce RF-GPT, a radio-frequency language model (RFLM) that utilizes the visual encoders of multimodal LLMs to process and understand RF spectrograms. In this framework, complex in-phase/quadrature (IQ) waveforms are mapped to time-frequency spectrograms and then passed to pretrained visual encoders. The resulting representations are injected as RF tokens into a decoder-only LLM, which generates RF-grounded answers, explanations, and structured outputs. To train RF-GPT, we perform supervised instruction fine-tuning of a pretrained multimodal LLM using a fully synthetic RF corpus. Standards-compliant waveform generators produce wideband scenes for six wireless technologies, from which we derive time-frequency spectrograms, exact configuration metadata, and dense captions. A text-only LLM then converts these captions into RF-grounded instruction-answer pairs, yielding roughly 120,000 RF scenes and 0.625 million instruction examples without any manual labeling. Across benchmarks for wideband modulation classification, overlap analysis, wireless-technology recognition, WLAN user counting, and 5G NR information extraction, RF-GPT achieves strong multi-task performance, whereas general-purpose VLMs with no RF grounding largely fail.

title: Interpreting Speaker Characteristics in the Dimensions of Self-Supervised Speech Features
comments: 5 pages, 7 figures, Published in IEEE Signal Processing Letters
summary: How do speech models trained through self-supervised learning structure their representations? Previous studies have looked at how information is encoded in feature vectors across different layers. But few studies have considered whether speech characteristics are captured \textit{within} individual dimensions of SSL features. In this paper, we specifically look at speaker information using PCA on utterance-averaged representations. For a range of SSL models, we find that the principal dimension that explains most variance encodes pitch and associated characteristics like gender. Other individual principal dimensions correlate with intensity, noise levels, the second formant, and higher frequency characteristics. We then use synthesis analyses to show that the dimensions for most characteristics are isolated from each other's influence. We further show that characteristics can be changed by manipulating the corresponding dimensions.
comment: 5 pages, 7 figures, Published in IEEE Signal Processing Letters

title: Joint Training Scattering Matrix Learning and Channel Estimation for Beyond-Diagonal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
summary: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) generalizes the conventional diagonal RIS (D-RIS) by introducing tunable inter-element connections, offering enhanced wave manipulation capabilities. However, realizing the advantages of BD-RIS requires accurate channel state information (CSI), whose acquisition becomes significantly more challenging due to the increased number of channel coefficients, leading to prohibitively large pilot training overhead in BD-RIS-aided multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Existing studies reduce pilot overhead by exploiting the channel correlations induced by the Kronecker-product or multi-linear structure of BD-RIS-aided channels, which neglect the spatial correlation among antennas and the statistical correlation across RIS-user channels. In this paper, we propose a learning-based channel estimation framework, namely the joint training scattering matrix learning and channel estimation framework (JTSMLCEF), which jointly optimizes the BD-RIS training scattering matrix and estimates the cascaded channels in an end-to-end manner to achieve accurate channel estimation and reduce the pilot overhead. The proposed JTSMLCEF follows a two-phase channel estimation protocol to enable adaptive training scattering matrix optimization with a training scattering matrix optimizer (TSMO) and cascaded channel estimation with a dual-attention channel estimator (DACE). Specifically, the DACE is designed with intra-user and inter-user attention modules to capture the multi-dimensional correlations in multi-user cascaded channels. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of JTSMLCEF. Compared with the current state-of-the-art method, it reduces the pilot overhead by $80\%$ while further reducing the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) by $82.6\%$ and $92.5\%$ in indoor and urban micro-cell (UMi) scenarios, respectively.

title: Beyond the Flat-Spike: Adaptive Sparse CCA for Decaying and Unbalanced Signals
comments: 16 pages, 7 figures; accepted by IEEE TSP
summary: Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SCCA) is a fundamental statistical tool for identifying linear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-view data. While minimax theory establishes an optimal sample complexity scaling additively with the sparsity levels of the canonical vectors, computationally efficient algorithms typically suffer from a suboptimal multiplicative dependence. This computational-statistical gap is intrinsically tied to worst-case ``flat'' signal assumptions. In practice, however, multi-view signals frequently exhibit structured energy concentration, such as a power-law decay. To exploit this structural concentration and bypass the worst-case bottleneck, we propose Bilateral Spectral Energy Pursuit (Bi-SEP). Operating directly on the cross-covariance matrix, Bi-SEP is a stagewise adaptive algorithm that utilizes a proxy refinement step to dynamically track and capture cross-view signal energy. Theoretically, we establish a profile-adaptive sample complexity bound governed by the coupled energy profiles of the two views. Notably, under power-law decay models, we reveal a synergistic phase transition: the optimal linear sample complexity is attainable provided that the aggregate decay rate of the two views is sufficiently large. This result demonstrates that a highly concentrated signal in one view allows the model to accommodate a completely flat signal in its partner. Numerical experiments validate our theoretical findings, illustrating the advantages of Bi-SEP in structured, non-flat signal regimes.
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures; accepted by IEEE TSP

title: Dynamic Quantum-Assisted Co-Design of Controller and Lyapunov Candidate Parameters for Nonlinear Systems
summary: This paper proposes a dynamic quantum-assisted co-design framework for nonlinear closed-loop systems in which controller parameters and Lyapunov candidate parameters are redesigned jointly at successive decision epochs. Unlike conventional nonlinear control designs that typically tune controller gains offline and perform stability analysis separately, the proposed method embeds performance improvement and sample-based Lyapunov verification within a unified online optimization loop. The main novelty is a two-step computational structure that first contracts the continuous admissible search region around the current operating condition using a Black-Hole calibration procedure and then constructs a finite binary representation only over this calibrated region. The encoded objective is obtained from sampled nonlinear closed-loop evaluations and approximated by a local quadratic pseudo-Boolean surrogate, enabling an Ising-type Hamiltonian representation suitable for quantum-assisted optimization. Quantum imaginary time evolution is then used to explore the encoded Hamiltonian, and the resulting candidate bitstrings are decoded into continuous controller and Lyapunov parameters. To reduce dependence on the surrogate model, the decoded candidates are re-evaluated using the original nonlinear closed-loop cost and Lyapunov penalties before the final update is applied. The framework can accommodate sampled forms of different Lyapunov decay specifications by modifying the corresponding penalty and is numerically evaluated on first-order nonlinear consensus, second-order nonlinear consensus, and induction motor drive control examples. The implementation code used to generate the reported results is available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DQCLS-NS}{GitHub}.

title: Coupling-Aware Pinching-Antenna Radiation for Heterogeneous NOMA Users
summary: Pinching-antennas systems (PASS) offer reconfigurable wireless channels via low-cost dielectric mediums by creating line-of-sight (LoS) communication links. Most of the existing PASS cover mechanisms of equal power pinching antennas for conventional bit-based communication, whereas flexible radiation control remains largely unexplored, particularly for heterogeneous semantic and bit users. In this paper, we investigate the performance of semantic communication (SC) using an adjustable radiation model over PASS, where the coupling strength between the dielectric waveguide and each pinching antenna is determined by the antenna-waveguide spacing. Specifically, the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted heterogeneous users are served by multiple pinching antennas using spacing-controlled adjustable radiation ratios. Uunder this setting, we maximize the semantic spectral efficiency (SE) subject to the bit-user quality of service (QoS) requirement, successive interference cancellation (SIC) feasibility, and the minimum adjacent antennas spacing constraint. An alternating optimization (AO) approach optimizes users power allocation and positions of pinching antennas. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proportional power PASS model in providing higher semantic SE in different geometrical and numerical settings compared to conventional benchmark schemes.

title: Large Language Models over Networks: Collaborative Intelligence under Resource Constraints
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming society, powering applications from smartphone assistants to autonomous driving. Yet cloud-based LLM services alone cannot serve a growing class of applications, including those operating under intermittent connectivity, sub-second latency budgets, data-residency constraints, or sustained high-volume inference. On-device deployment is in turn constrained by limited computation and memory. No single endpoint can deliver high-quality service across this spectrum. This article focuses on collaborative intelligence, a paradigm in which multiple independent LLMs distributed across device and cloud endpoints collaborate at the task level through natural language or structured messages. Such collaboration strives for superior response quality under heterogeneous resource constraints spanning computation, memory, communication, and cost across network tiers. We present collaborative inference along two complementary and composable dimensions: vertical device-cloud collaboration and horizontal multi-agent collaboration, which can be combined into hybrid topologies in practice. We then examine learning to collaborate, addressing the training of routing policies and the development of cooperative capabilities among LLMs. Finally, we identify open research challenges including scaling under resource heterogeneity and trustworthy collaborative intelligence.

title: ForcingDAS: Unified and Robust Data Assimilation via Diffusion Forcing
summary: Data assimilation (DA) estimates the state of an evolving dynamical system from noisy, partial observations, and is widely used in scientific simulation as well as weather and climate science. In practice, filtering methods rely on frame-to-frame transition models. However, these models are fragile when observations are non-Markovian (when they form only a partial slice of a higher-dimensional latent state as in real-world weather data): they tend to accumulate errors over long horizons. At the same time, learned DA methods typically commit to a single regime, either filtering (nowcasting, real-time forecasting) or smoothing (retrospective reanalysis), which splits what should be a shared prior across application-specific pipelines. To address both issues, we introduce ForcingDAS, a unified and robust DA framework. Built on Diffusion Forcing with an independent noise level assigned to each frame, ForcingDAS learns a joint-trajectory prior instead of frame-to-frame transitions. This allows it to capture long-horizon temporal dependencies and reduce error accumulation. In addition, the same trained model spans the full filtering to smoothing spectrum at inference time. Specifically, nowcasting, fixed-lag smoothing, and batch reanalysis are selected through the inference schedule alone, without retraining. We evaluate ForcingDAS on 2D Navier-Stokes vorticity, precipitation nowcasting, and global atmospheric state estimation. Across all settings, a single model is competitive with or outperforms both learned and classical baselines that are specialized for individual regimes, with the largest gains observed on real-world weather benchmarks.

title: Buffer-Parameterized Machine Learning Surrogate Models for Cross-Technology Signal Integrity Analysis and Optimization
comments: 12 pages, 16 figures, 7 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: Signal integrity (SI) analysis in printed circuit board (PCB) interconnects faces increasing complexity due to diverse integrated circuit (IC) buffer technologies, varying operating conditions, and manufacturing tolerances. Existing machine learning (ML) surrogate models for the prediction of SI metrics such as the inner eye contour, eye-height (EH), eye-width (EW), and transient waveform features often rely on fixed buffer parameters, limiting the adaptability across design and technology variations. This paper introduces a buffer-parameterized ML surrogate modeling methodology capable of handling cross-technology variations without retraining by treating IC buffer characteristics, e.g., clock frequency, supply voltage, rise/fall times, jitter, and internal resistors and capacitors, as model inputs in addition to the PCB parameters. To identify the optimal surrogate architecture for this high-dimensional space, tree-based methods (RFR/GBM), kernel methods (SVR/KRR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and neural networks are compared. The buffer-parameterized approach is validated using a complex interconnect with a total of 44 design parameters. In addition to demonstrating strong generalization, the results show that neural networks outperform other ML models on large datasets, while the anisotropic GPR excels in low-data regimes. Finally, the practical value of the ML surrogate models is demonstrated through a cross-technology design space exploration and optimization scenario, which indicates large computational speedups for eye mask compliance checking compared to simulation.
